source.title: Learning Rate Dropout
source.authors: Huang-Xing Lin; Weihong Zeng; Yihong Zhuang; Xing-Hao Ding; Yue Huang; J. Paisley

record.tranche_reason: The study compares standard dropout with no regularization and reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy, using the same general intervention as V6 in a different experimental setting.
record.gate_note: The study's main intervention, learning rate dropout (LRD), is not a V6 intervention. Rows are limited to its reported standard-dropout comparisons, which directly bear on V6.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares standard dropout with no dropout and adaptive optimizers with SGDM using held-out classification accuracy. These are the interventions and measures in V6 and V4, despite being secondary to its proposed learning rate dropout method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' secondary standard-dropout findings: dropout can improve generalization, but its retain probability requires care in convolutional networks. Their main conclusion is that learning rate dropout accelerates training and improves generalization across classification, segmentation, and detection.
record.recipe_differences: The study includes standard dropout as a comparison alongside its proposed learning-rate-dropout method; it evaluates ResNet-34 on CIFAR-10 rather than the broader settings summarized in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Standard-dropout retain probability changes the reported Adam test accuracy; the authors state that performance is sensitive to its choice.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning rate dropout improves training speed and held-out performance across several tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly suppressing parameter updates can improve optimization and generalization; this intervention differs from standard hidden-unit dropout in V6.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the test-accuracy comparisons. The dropout-rate sweep reports results only for Adam.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. The remaining tables and figures concern LRD, other regularizers, or tasks outside the tested V6 standard-dropout comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.

Standard dropout in fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, and removing dropout and weight decay together with augmentation. The supplied text reports worse convergence with stronger dropout but does not provide readable training-accuracy values establishing underfitting.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence and retraining.

missing.what: Direct optimizer comparisons without LRD: SGDM/RMSprop/Adam/AMSGrad/RAdam accuracy is 97.82/98.06/97.88/97.88/97.97% on MNIST, 95.30/92.71/93.05/93.31/94.24% on CIFAR-10, and 79.09/70.21/72.55/73.91/71.81% on CIFAR-100. Record adaptive-versus-SGDM contrasts and the limited tuning protocol.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4 or V6. No uncertainty estimates accompany the tabulated comparisons. The record incorrectly marks V4 untested. LRD-only improvements do not establish V6; the record explicitly declares those results omitted.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Very small training sets; fully connected classifiers; explicit evidence of underfitting; data augmentation with dropout and weight decay removed together.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: ResNet-34 on CIFAR-10, Adam, retain probabilities 0.7 and 0.6.
relationships.reason: The gain shrinks to 0.29 percentage points at 0.7 and reverses to a 0.16-point loss at 0.6, demonstrating configuration dependence (R6, R7).
relationships.display_finding: With learning rate dropout, a 0.7 probability of keeping parameter updates raised accuracy by 0.29 percentage points; a 0.6 probability lowered it by 0.16 percentage points. Uncertainty was not quantified.
